ceasefire.name: Ceasefire / de-escalation (offset path)
ceasefire.description: The baseline disruption regime is forced to end in Dec 2026 (month 2); markets reprice quickly. Use to see which costs reverse and which persist (OMC recoupment, expectations, reserves).

combined_stress.name: Simultaneous stress - oil escalation + global tightening
combined_stress.description: Oil escalation and global tightening together from Nov 2026. Common shocks enter once each, through their own channels; correlation of residual innovations is not added on top.

food_stress.name: Domestic food-supply stress (2027 monsoon failure)
food_stress.description: Food supply shock of +6pp (annualised food inflation) from Jul 2027 (month 9) for 5 months, on top of the reference path. Tests expectations de-anchoring and the RBI look-through choice.

global_tightening.name: Global demand weakness + US financial tightening
global_tightening.description: From Nov 2026: US10Y +80bp, dollar +5%, risk-off +1.5 sd, world demand gap -1.5pp, each persisting 9 months then decaying. Oil anchor falls with weaker demand through the oil_gdem_beta channel (a demand-driven oil move, unlike the supply escalation).

oil_escalation.name: Oil escalation - Strait of Hormuz disruption (supply shock)
oil_escalation.description: Escalation on top of the current regime from Nov 2026: Hormuz transit disrupted. Oil anchor +USD40/bbl, freight +USD6, cracks +USD8, 3% physical crude shortfall for a forced 3 months, after which the escalation layer ends with 20%/month hazard. Risk-off +1.0 sd on onset. Shock type = SUPPLY disruption (not demand-led), so global demand does not rise with oil.

reference.name: Reference path (current disruption regime persists, resolves at random)
reference.description: No new shock. Starts from the October 2026 state: Brent ~USD117 under an ongoing Gulf supply-disruption regime that ends with a monthly hazard (central 12%/month). This is the comparison baseline, not a forecast.

prompts: It is October 2027 and INR is at 90, CPI at 4%, and growth 7.5%. What did the model miss?
It is October 2027 and INR is at 115 and the RBI has used USD150bn. Which channel was underweighted?
The 'best-looking' policy in the comparison failed in reality. Which cost was hidden from the model?
model_weaknesses: BIAS TOWARD FISCAL ABSORPTION: the 10Y yield does not feed back into the output gap, and there is no sovereign-rating, crowding-out or financial-stability channel. 'Budget compensates OMCs' therefore looks cheaper for growth than it may be.
Capital flows are the weakest block: FPI coefficients and the residual plug are judgmental; the RBI dollar-deposit window reversal is not modelled.
FX depth is illustrative: INR paths scale with it. Treat INR levels as conditional, not predictive.
Single representative auto fuel and Delhi VAT; no state VAT responses, no LPG price changes.
No bank/NBFC/insurer balance sheets: a bond sell-off cannot create financial-stability feedback.
Pre-sample histories are synthetic: year-on-year CPI and GDP over the first 12 months carry artificial base effects.
Actors follow fixed rules; real policymakers mix options, communicate, and react to politics (state elections).
Oil regime hazard is judgmental; diplomacy and military events are not modelled, only their price consequences.
strongest_countercase: India's starting buffers (USD735bn reserves, 4.3% deficit path, low CAD at 0.5% of GDP in Q1) may absorb even a severe shock with less depreciation than modelled, especially if remittances and services stay strong.
missing_actors: State governments (VAT), OPEC+/Saudi spare capacity, US Treasury/Fed swap lines, IMF, Russia (discounted crude), China (demand).
